title: The Contractor Operations add-on: Jobs, a job’s page with its materials, time and costs so far, a visit’s work order, Dispatch, Estimates and the estimate builder, Item costs, Profit and Settings, on the web

items.path: Side menu → Contractor Operations (opens Jobs; Dispatch pops out, Estimates, Item costs and Profit for people who may see job costs, Settings for owners and admins)
items.by: add-on directory line in the prompt; CONTRACTOR_PLACES link each page

items.path: Add-ons → Contractor Operations → settings: what its settings are, with Open Contractor settings
Jobs → header: business name and what the page is for
Jobs → New job
Jobs → Pick your trade notice (owners and admins, while no trade is picked), with Pick your trade
Jobs → counts: Open, Late, On hold, Done this month (Open and Late filter the list)
Jobs → filters: All jobs, My jobs, Late
Jobs → Search jobs
Jobs → Show done and cancelled
Jobs → Board or List
items.by: contractor_list_jobs answers both: the board is the list grouped by status

items.path: Jobs → no jobs yet, or none match
Jobs → Board → a column per status, with how many
Jobs → Board → a job’s card: name, kind, customer, property, % done, deadline or days late, lead, why it’s on hold
Jobs → Board → a job’s card opens its page
items.by: contractor_get_job; the A job place links it

items.path: Jobs → List → each job: name, kind, trade and lead; status; customer and property; % done and phases done; deadline; next visit
Jobs → showing the first jobs only, search to find others
New job → Job name
New job → What kind of job: Service call or Project, with what each means
New job → Customer (search, from Contacts)
New job → Property: one of your properties by address (the customer’s first), or a new address
New job → Trade
New job → Job lead (someone else only for owners and admins)
New job → Starts and Deadline
New job → Work to do
New job → a project starts with these phases
items.by: contractor_open_job (phases, else the starter phases); contractor_overview (settings.phases)

items.path: New job → Start the job (opens its page)
A job → back to Jobs
A job → header: name, status, kind, days late, trade, why it’s on hold or cancelled
A job → Status (New, Scheduled, In progress, On hold, Done, Cancelled)
A job → On hold or Cancelled → Why
A job → Done while required items are left → what’s left, by visit, each visit opening its work order
items.by: contractor_set_job_status refuses and names what’s left; contractor_get_job (visits[].checklist); contractor_get_work_order (items)

items.path: A job → Done while required items are left → finish them first, or ask an owner or admin
items.by: the refusal says the same; contractor_overview (may.skipChecks)

items.path: A job → Done while required items are left → Why, and Mark it done anyway (owners and admins)
A job → Book a visit (for the job, its customer filled in; its work order then opens)
items.by: book_appointment (customRecordId: the job); contractor_start_work_order; the A work order place

items.path: A job → Notes, files and tasks (the job’s record page)
items.by: core's record tools (find_records, notes, tasks, files) on the job's record

items.path: A job → Details: customer, property, starts, deadline (and days left or late), work to do
A job → Details → customer and property open their pages
A job → Details → Edit
A job → Edit → name, customer, property (or a new address), trade, lead, starts, deadline, work to do
A job → Phases: each phase in order, with its number, start, deadline (days left or late) and when it was done
A job → Phases → how many are done
A job → Phases → none yet: Make it a project
A job → Phases → move a phase up or down
A job → Phases → a phase’s status (Not started, Started, Done)
A job → Phases → a phase’s % done
A job → Phases → edit a phase: name, starts, deadline
A job → Phases → remove a phase, asked first
A job → Phases → Add a phase (the first makes it a project)
A job → Visits: each visit’s time and title, where it stands (scheduled, on the way, started, done), its crew and its checklist’s progress
A job → Visits → a visit opens its work order
items.by: contractor_get_work_order (the visit’s appointmentId, from contractor_get_job); the A work order place

items.path: A job → % done, with how it’s worked out (from its phases, or set by hand)
A job → % done → set it by hand (a service call)
A job → Team: the job lead, and everyone else on it
A job → Team → take someone off
A job → Team → Add to the team
A job → Budget and price (people who may see job costs): price, labor, materials, other, budget, labor hours, planned profit, margin (red below 20%)
A job → Budget and price → Edit: price, labor, materials, other costs, labor hours
Settings → Your trades
Settings → Start from a trade’s starter phases
items.by: do_addon_save_settings settings.phases (the trade’s starters, from the Settings place)

items.path: Settings → Phases for a new project: each in order, move up or down, remove
Settings → what new projects start with when no list is set
Settings → add a phase
Settings → Save settings
Jobs → N estimates are waiting for your OK, with Review (people who may OK them)
A job → Estimates: each one’s number or Draft, customer, status, whether it waits for an OK or has one, title, options or the one picked, day and total (opens it)
A job → Estimates → New estimate (people who may see job costs)
items.by: contractor_write_estimate (jobId; its customer is who it goes to)

items.path: Estimates → header and New estimate
Estimates → filters: All, Waiting for an OK
Estimates → each estimate: number or Draft, customer, status, Waiting for an OK or OK given, title, job, options or the one picked, day, total (opens its builder)
Estimates → none yet, or none waiting
An estimate → back to its job, or to Estimates
items.by: the A job and Estimates places

items.path: An estimate → header: New estimate or Estimate for <customer>, Draft, saved or not saved yet
items.by: contractor_get_estimate (estimate.state, person); contractor_write_estimate saves it whole

items.path: An estimate → Save
An estimate → Send (held while it waits for an OK)
items.by: contractor_send_estimate, refused with why while it needs an OK

items.path: An estimate → notice: you can’t bill here, so you can read it but not save or send
items.by: contractor_get_estimate (may.bill); the write and send tools are refused the same way

items.path: An estimate → someone saved it while you were editing → Load their version
items.by: contractor_write_estimate saves over the newest (baseRevision left out); contractor_get_estimate reads it

items.path: An estimate → Customer: name, email and phone; pick one, or Change before it’s first saved
items.by: contractor_get_estimate (person); contractor_write_estimate (personId, or the job’s customer); find_people

items.path: An estimate → For job: the job it’s for (opens it)
An estimate → What it’s for (its title)
An estimate → Lines → One price or options (good, better, best): Offer options, a tab each, Add an option, Called, Take this option off
items.by: contractor_write_estimate (options: one, or two or three named); contractor_get_estimate (estimate.options)

items.path: An estimate → each line: What it is, Description
An estimate → each line: Labor, Material or Other
An estimate → each line: How many (hours for labor)
An estimate → each line: Cost (what one costs the business)
An estimate → each line: Markup % (sets the price from the cost)
items.by: contractor_write_estimate (lines[].unitPriceCents, worked out from the cost and the markup); contractor_get_estimate (estimating.markupBp)

items.path: An estimate → each line: Price
An estimate → each line: its amount, and its profit
An estimate → each line: Remove
An estimate → Add labor (hours at the business’s hourly price and cost)
An estimate → Add a line
An estimate → From your price list (the item’s price, and its cost from Item costs)
An estimate → Take off: nothing, a % or an amount
An estimate → Notes for the customer
An estimate → Costs and profit: price before tax, labor (and hours), materials, other, cost, profit, margin (red under the lowest margin)
items.by: contractor_get_estimate (check.options: price, labor, materials, other, cost, profit, margin, hours)

items.path: An estimate → Costs and profit → each option’s margin, side by side
An estimate → Costs and profit → it clears the lowest margin, or why it waits for an OK (an option under it, or lines with no cost)
items.by: contractor_get_estimate (check.needsOk, lowest, uncosted, minMarginBp); contractor_write_estimate answers the same

items.path: An estimate → Ask for an OK (owners and admins are told on Home and their phones)
An estimate → an OK was asked for by <name>
An estimate → OK it (owners and admins), with an optional note
An estimate → OK given by <name>, good until it changes
An estimate → Totals: subtotal, discount, tax, total (the open option’s)
items.by: contractor_write_estimate answers the total; contractor_get_estimate (estimate.totals, options[].totals)

items.path: An estimate → Deposit: ask for one, as a percent or an amount
An estimate → Good until
An estimate → Send dialog: by email, by text, a line to go with it; Send or Not yet
items.by: contractor_send_estimate (channels, message), on a Confirm card

items.path: An estimate that has gone out → its number, customer and status; it can’t be changed here
An estimate that has gone out → Open it in Money
An estimate that has gone out → each option’s costs, profit and margin, and the one they picked
Money → an estimate built here → Costs and profit panel (people who may see job costs): each option’s cost, profit and margin
Money → an estimate built here → Open the estimate builder
Item costs → header, and where items are added (Settings → Products)
items.by: the Item costs place; manage_product adds items

items.path: Item costs → Search
items.by: contractor_list_item_costs answers every item to look through

items.path: Item costs → each item: name, price, cost, kind, margin (red under the lowest margin)
Item costs → an item’s kind: Labor, Material or Other
Item costs → an item’s cost (empty takes it off), Save
Settings → Estimating: what it is, and that only owners and admins change it
Settings → Estimating → Lowest margin
Settings → Estimating → Starting markup
Settings → Estimating → Labor, what you charge an hour
Settings → Estimating → Labor, what an hour costs you
Settings → Estimating → Save
A work order → back to its job
A work order → header: when the visit is, where it stands, its title and its checklist’s progress
A work order → Open in Calendar (the visit itself: its time and status, move or cancel it)
items.by: get_appointment, reschedule_appointment, cancel_appointment, update_job_status; the Calendar place

items.path: A work order → notice: the visit was cancelled, or its job is done or cancelled, so it can only be read
items.by: contractor_get_work_order (visit.status, job.status); a change is refused with why

items.path: A work order → No work order yet, with Start its work order
A work order → Job: the job (opens it) with its status, customer, property and work to do
A work order → Job → customer and property open their pages
A work order → Instructions and What to bring
A work order → Instructions and What to bring → Edit, then Save
A work order → Checklist: how many required items are left, or that it’s ready
A work order → Checklist → each item: what it is, Required, a tick or a photo, who did it, or that it was passed over and why
A work order → Checklist → nothing on it yet
A work order → Checklist → tick or untick an item
A work order → Checklist → a photo item → Add a photo, or replace it (taken or chosen on this device)
items.by: the photo comes from the person’s own device; contractor_set_checklist_item (fileId) marks it with a photo already in the job’s files

items.path: A work order → Checklist → a photo item → See the photo (opens it in the job’s files)
items.by: contractor_get_work_order (items[].file) names it; the picture itself isn’t read

items.path: A work order → Checklist → an item’s menu: Make it required or optional
A work order → Checklist → an item’s menu: untick a photo item
items.by: contractor_set_checklist_item (done: false), on a Confirm card

items.path: A work order → Checklist → an item’s menu: Remove, asked first
A work order → Checklist → add an item: what it is, a tick or a photo, Required
A work order → Checklist → note: the job can’t be marked Done while a required item is left
items.by: the A work order place; contractor_set_job_status refuses the same way

items.path: A work order → Who’s going → Crew: one of the business’s crews, or none
items.by: contractor_list_crews; contractor_set_visit_crew (crewId, or null), on a Confirm card

items.path: A work order → Who’s going → the people on the visit
A work order → Who’s going → someone in the crew is busy or off then: why, with Put them on anyway
items.by: contractor_set_visit_crew answers the warnings; acknowledgeWarnings puts them on anyway

items.path: A work order → Subcontractors: each one’s name (opens the contact) and company, when they were texted or that they can’t be, and whether their work is done
A work order → Subcontractors → Their work is done (the office marks it)
A work order → Subcontractors → take one off the visit
A work order → Subcontractors → Add a subcontractor (search, from Contacts)
A work order → Subcontractors → Text the details, to all of them or to one
items.by: contractor_text_visit_subs (personIds for one), on a Confirm card

items.path: A work order → Text the details → a line of your own, then Send
A work order → Text the details → in quiet hours: why it waits, and Send again to send anyway
items.by: contractor_text_visit_subs is refused with why; acknowledgeQuietHours once the person says to send anyway

items.path: A work order → Text the details → who wasn’t texted, and why
Dispatch → header: what the page is for
Dispatch → the day: the day before, pick a day, the day after, Today
Dispatch → the day’s name, and whether it’s today
Dispatch → no visits on jobs that day
Dispatch → Nobody on it yet: the day’s visits nobody is on
Dispatch → a column per person (the person looking first): their visits that day, and how many
Dispatch → a visit: its time, where it stands (scheduled, on the way, started, done), job, customer and property, crew, subcontractors done, checklist progress
items.by: contractor_get_dispatch (each visit: stage, job, customer, property, crew, subs, checklist)

items.path: Dispatch → a visit opens its work order
items.by: contractor_get_work_order; the A work order place

items.path: Dispatch → showing the first visits only
Dispatch → Needs a visit: open jobs with nothing booked, each with its status, days late, customer, property and deadline
Dispatch → Needs a visit → Open the job (to book its visit)
Settings → Checklist for a new visit: what it is
Settings → Checklist → Start from a trade’s starter checklist
items.by: do_addon_save_settings settings.checklist (the trade’s starters, from the Settings place)

items.path: Settings → Checklist → each item in order: a tick or a photo, Required on or off, move up or down, remove
items.by: do_addon_save_settings settings.checklist (label, kind, required, in order)

items.path: Settings → Checklist → what new visits start with when no list is set
Settings → Checklist → add an item: what it is, a tick or a photo, Required
Settings → Crews: what a crew is, and each crew’s name and who’s in it
Settings → Crews → none yet
Settings → Crews → New crew
Settings → Crews → Edit a crew
Settings → Crews → a crew’s dialog: Name
Settings → Crews → a crew’s dialog: People on your team (tick each)
Settings → Crews → a crew’s dialog: Subcontractors: add one from Contacts, take one off
Settings → Crews → a crew’s dialog: Save
Settings → Crews → Archive a crew, asked first
Settings → Crews → Show archived, and Bring back
items.by: contractor_list_crews (includeArchived); contractor_archive_crew (archived: false), on a Confirm card

items.path: A job → Visits → a visit that’s still missing materials says how many, in red
A job → Materials: how many are still missing, or that everything is here
A job → Materials → none yet

A job → Materials → each material: its name, where it stands (To order, On order, Here, Used up), how much is here of what’s needed, what’s short or left, when it’s expected, where it’s from, the visit it’s for, whether it came from an estimate, and its note
items.by: contractor_list_materials (each material: state, needed, delivered, short, left, expectedOn, supplier, appointmentId, fromEstimate, note)

items.path: A job → Materials → what one costs, or that it has no cost yet (people who may see job costs)
A job → Materials → Mark ordered, Mark delivered or Mark used (one press moves it along)
items.by: contractor_update_material (ordered, delivered or used, each the total so far)

items.path: A job → Materials → a material’s menu: Edit, and Remove, asked first
items.by: contractor_update_material; contractor_remove_material, on a Confirm card

items.path: A job → Materials → Add a material
A job → Materials → a material’s dialog: From your price list (people who can see it)
items.by: get_settings (area products) lists the price list; contractor_add_material (productId)

items.path: A job → Materials → a material’s dialog: what it is, and what it’s counted in
A job → Materials → a material’s dialog: Needed, Ordered and Delivered (and Used, Wasted and Returned on one that’s on the list)
items.by: contractor_add_material (needed, ordered, delivered); contractor_update_material (all six, each the total so far)

items.path: A job → Materials → a material’s dialog: the visit it’s for, or any visit
items.by: contractor_add_material and contractor_update_material (appointmentId, null for any visit); contractor_get_job (visits)

items.path: A job → Materials → a material’s dialog: Supplier and Expected on
A job → Materials → a material’s dialog: what one costs (people who may see job costs)
items.by: contractor_add_material (unitCostCents); contractor_set_material_cost, on a Confirm card

items.path: A job → Materials → a material’s dialog: Note
A job → Materials → a material’s dialog: Save
A job → Materials → what they cost: planned, taken so far, and how many have no cost yet (people who may see job costs)
items.by: contractor_list_materials (costing: plannedCents, takenCents, uncosted; only for contractor.costs)

items.path: A work order → Materials for this visit: the job’s materials it needs (its own, and the ones for any visit), with the same marks, menu, Add and dialog as on the job, never with a cost
A work order → Materials → See all the job’s materials
Dispatch → a visit that’s still missing materials says how many, in red
Settings → Missing materials: what it is, and who is told
Settings → Missing materials → Tell them: how long before the visit, or never
A job → Time: the hours tracked (work, travel and breaks), and how many people are on the clock now
A job → Time → none yet, and when it starts
items.by: contractor_list_time (empty); the A job place says what starts and stops time

items.path: A job → Time → Take a break, or Back to work (while you’re working or on a break on a visit)
A job → Time → each stretch: whose it is, travel, work or break, whether it’s running, from when to when, the visit it was on, and how long
A job → Time → a stretch stopped on its own after 12 hours says so, and who fixes it
A job → Time → a fixed stretch says who fixed it and why
A job → Time → a stretch’s menu: Fix, and Remove, which asks why (people who may fix time)
items.by: contractor_fix_time; contractor_remove_time (reason), each on a Confirm card

items.path: A job → Time → Show all, or Show fewer
items.by: contractor_list_time answers with every stretch (the newest 500)

items.path: A job → Time → Add time (people who may fix time)
A job → Time → the time dialog: Who (when adding)
A job → Time → the time dialog: What (Work, Travel or Break)
A job → Time → the time dialog: Visit, or no visit (when adding)
A job → Time → the time dialog: Started and Ended, on the business’s clock
items.by: contractor_add_time and contractor_fix_time (startedAt, endedAt, as ISO moments)

items.path: A job → Time → the time dialog: Why
A job → Time → the time dialog: Save
A work order → Time on this visit: the visit’s hours and stretches, with Take a break or Back to work, and the same Fix, Remove and Add time as on the job
items.by: contractor_list_time (appointmentId); contractor_set_break; contractor_fix_time, contractor_remove_time and contractor_add_time (appointmentId)

items.path: A work order → Time → See all the job’s time
A job → Costs so far (people who may see job costs): Labor, Materials, Other costs and Total cost, each planned, so far and heading for
A job → Costs so far → Labor hours: planned, so far and heading for
A job → Costs so far → Price, Profit and Margin: planned, so far and heading for
A job → Costs so far → heading over what was planned, or under the lowest margin
A job → Costs so far → on track for what was planned, or finished
A job → Costs so far → no price set, time or materials with no cost yet, and how heading for is worked out
items.by: contractor_get_job_costing (priceCents, uncostedHours, uncostedMaterials); its description says how heading for is worked out

items.path: A job → Costs so far → Labor by person: each person’s hours and what they cost
A job → Costs so far → Other costs: each with its day, note and amount, or none yet
A job → Costs so far → Other costs → Add a cost
A job → Costs so far → Add a cost: What it was for, Amount, Day and Note, and Save
A job → Costs so far → Other costs → Remove one, asked first
Profit → header: what the page is for
Profit → Which jobs: done this month, last month, this quarter, this year or all time, or the open jobs
Profit → Split: by job, customer, crew or service
Profit → the days it covers, and how the jobs are counted
items.by: contractor_get_profit (from, to); its description says how done and open jobs count, and which crew a job counts for

items.path: Profit → Price, Cost, Profit and Margin for all of them together
Profit → no jobs to count
Profit → each row: its name, how many jobs, price, cost, profit, margin (red under the lowest margin) and labor hours
Profit → a job’s row opens the job, and a customer’s opens the customer
items.by: contractor_get_job or get_person, by the row’s key

items.path: Profit → showing the first jobs only
Settings → What an hour costs you (people who may see job costs): what it is, and what counts for someone with no cost of their own
Settings → What an hour costs you → each person’s cost per hour
items.by: contractor_list_labor_costs (people); contractor_set_labor_cost (costCents; null takes it off), on a Confirm card

items.path: Settings → What an hour costs you → Save (owners and admins)
